cards.shapeChange: Before, the card let each tablet keep a list of claimed tokens. Now only the Game record holds it; a tablet draws what it is sent and asks at each tap, so a delete or reset leaves no stale list.
cards.atAShow: A GM deletes a transaction. The engine frees the token, but every tablet that stays connected keeps refusing it as already scanned until someone reloads. A tablet that drops its connection during Reset All Scores comes back still holding the old claims, and refuses tokens the engine has cleared.
cards.whyItHappens: The engine decides which tokens are claimed, but each tablet holds a copy that only grows: added on scan, merged on reconnect, removed only when a scan fails. The engine's own messages also skip facts that change as a side effect of something else, such as a team created by a scan.
cards.designTerms: The Game record should own which tokens are claimed, read from the transactions. Delivery's interface is the one seam between a claim and a screen; each tablet is a Screens adapter drawing it. Today the tablet updates its copy with one hand-written step per message; a message with no step leaves it stale: no locality.

after.note: Only the Game record decides which tokens are claimed, from the transactions. Delivery sends it by one route, live or on reconnect; Lifecycle announces resets. The tablet keeps no list: it draws the fact and asks at each tap. Or: each job sends its own.

cards.shapeChange: Before, the card left the record and updates with the music service. Now Equipment keeps one dated record of each thing the room does and Delivery sends each change by one route, so every panel sees outages and recoveries.
cards.atAShow: If the lighting system or the music player is down when the engine starts, the lighting and music panels stay disabled until someone reloads the tablet. If the music player dies mid-show, the health row turns red alone while the music card keeps its playing look and the progress bar keeps moving. A volume change on one tablet's audio panel never reaches the other tablets' sliders.
cards.whyItHappens: Each venue program has two facts about it: its health, in one shared health list, and its state, in its own record. The engine sends the health row when health changes, and sends a program's state only for a hand-written list of that program's events. An outage is on no list.
cards.designTerms: Equipment should own one dated record per thing the room does, behind one interface giving value, health and age, with the music player an adapter beneath. Delivery should own the one route: each fact built once for live and catch-up, labelled. Today each program's events are re-listed by hand; callers must know all: no locality.

after.note: Equipment keeps one dated record per thing the room does, health and state together. Delivery sends it by one route, live or on reconnect, so every panel, even one opened late, sees outages and recoveries. Or: each job sends its own facts; this fault returns.

cards.shapeChange: Before, the card let the code that reads each program own the engine's picture of it. Now Equipment owns one dated picture per thing the room does; Show runner reads it and keeps no copy; Delivery carries every correction.
cards.atAShow: A video stayed stopped for about 28 seconds because the engine held each message from the video player until the next one arrived. A false "video finished" can fire two seconds in, flipping the display back and restoring music. When the music player dies the engine still says playing and the controls stay dead until the next 15-second check. A cue with a 2-second video never completes.
cards.whyItHappens: The engine learns what VLC, the music player and the other programs are doing by reading their text or their stream of events into a saved copy that starts from a guess and carries no age. Re-reads are partial, and the video queue, cue timelines and health rows treat the copy as the program itself.
cards.designTerms: Equipment should own one picture per thing the room does, behind one interface giving value, health and age, checked against the program; VLC, the music player and a software stand-in are adapters at that seam. Show runner keeps none. Today the queue, timelines and health rows read each program's ageless copy directly: no locality.

after.note: The code that reads each program is the adapter beneath Equipment, which owns one dated picture per thing the room does. Show runner keeps no copy. Delivery carries each correction, dated. Or: one interface per program, nearer today's code, scattering questions about several programs.

cards.shapeChange: Before, the card's table of moments had no owner. Now Lifecycle owns it, alone moves the game and calls every reset; Delivery tells every screen and player device each moment as a fact, so none has to guess.
cards.atAShow: The GM ends the game and restarts the engine; the ended game comes back as the current one and player scans keep landing in it. When the game ends, a tablet that reconnects loses its history and the wall scoreboard goes blank. A once-only cue spent in game one stays spent in game two.
cards.whyItHappens: Game start, end, reset, engine restart, tablet reload and reconnect, the game's boundaries, each have their own code on each device. No table says, for each fact and each copy, whether a boundary clears it, keeps it or fetches it again, and no message announces one; screens guess a boundary from a changed session id.
cards.designTerms: Lifecycle should own the table of moments against facts and the one interface that moves a game from one moment to the next by that table; it alone calls every part's reset, and Delivery sends each moment as a fact. Today the session, cue, reset and tablet modules each hold their own cases: no locality.

after.note: Lifecycle holds one table saying what each moment does to each fact. It alone moves the game and calls every reset. Delivery sends each moment as a versioned fact every screen compares. Or: each part reads the table itself; only a test shows all did.

Later, Reset All Scores sends every tablet and the TV the old transaction list, so cleared evidence comes back on the wall. The cues now hear each video and clock event twice, and the Display row stays red until Check Now.
cards.whyItHappens: Starting the engine and rebuilding it after a reset are two separate hand-written lists. The start connects the parts in one order with one set of programs; the reset connects them in the other order with a shorter set, and connects some a second time.
cards.designTerms: Lifecycle should own the one path engine start and Reset System share, and alone call each part's reset; a starting point above every part should own the one list the engine is built from, under Engine instance's names. Today both do it by hand, each knowing every part and the order: no locality.

cards.shapeChange: Before, the card had each engine part describe its facts. Now Delivery builds each fact once, for catch-up and live change, and a restore after a reload is sent like a change, so the History badge and clock wake.
cards.atAShow: A GM reloads a tablet mid-game. The History badge stays hidden until the next scan, and a rebuilt admin panel can show the clock as --:-- until the next change. The device list flips between every device ever seen and only those connected now, depending on which message came last.
cards.whyItHappens: For each fact the engine has one piece of code that writes the catch-up snapshot a tablet gets on connect and another that writes the live message, and six places send the catch-up with hand-picked contents. The tablet applies each by a different rule, and a restore after a reload sends screens none of the signals they watch for.
cards.designTerms: Delivery should own one builder per fact, serving the catch-up snapshot and the live message from each deciding part's changes; Lifecycle's restore sends the same, and Screens draws only what that interface defines. Today the snapshot builder is shallow: a caller hands it every module, and five tablet adapters reshape its output: no locality.

after.note: Delivery builds each fact once, so the catch-up and the live message carry one fact in one shape, with its label. A restore after a reload is sent like a change. Screens draws each fact one way. Or: each job sends its own facts.

cards.shapeChange: Before, the card's reply part saved and answered. Now the Game record saves and Answering replies through one door for all devices, with one list of reply words, so a batch with no game gets one answer: stored or refused.
cards.atAShow: Player devices upload their queued scans while no game exists. The engine answers "processed", stores nothing, and both devices delete the scans. A GM's scan that can never succeed comes back as a vague error, so the tablet resends it at every reconnect with a pop-up message each time. A slow Reset System reports failure and the new game is skipped.
cards.whyItHappens: The engine answers before, or without, saving the fact it reports; calls an unsaved batch processed; returns some failures as a named outcome and others as a vague error; and confirms a command by the command's name alone, so two quick presses cannot be told apart. Each device then decides for itself what a reply means.
cards.designTerms: Answering should own one interface, one request in and one reply out, web requests and the live connection its two adapters; the outcome words are one closed list every device reads as data; the Game record answers after the save. Today three reply shapes leave each device its own rule: no locality.

after.note: Every reply names its request and says whether it is final and whether anything was stored. The Game record saves first, then answers through Answering: one door and one list of outcome words for every device. Or: each device asks which scans are stored.

cards.atAShow: On 2026-09-15 a unit test killed the live show's video player on the blue machine's code. In this code the same test run kills the live engine's watcher for the video player and overwrites the files that say which programs are running. A killed engine leaves a full-screen player behind. Twenty-one groups of tests open a browser on the show TV. The operator's health check says "VLC not found" while the player runs.
cards.whyItHappens: The engine finds and ends its helper programs by fixed file names and by searching the whole machine for programs by name, as if it were the only engine on the machine. The tests take over whatever display, sound and Bluetooth exist; that a test is safe is claimed in a note in the code, never checked.
cards.designTerms: Engine instance should own every name this engine holds, behind one interface; the settings file, a test's settings and a preview's settings are adapters at its seam, and a starting point builds every part under those names. Today no such seam exists: modules write fixed shared files and kill by machine-wide name search: no locality.

after.note: One Engine instance holds every name an engine owns, and a starting point builds the parts from one list, under those names. A test run and the designer's preview engine are engines too, so each ends only what it started. No machine-wide kill remains.
